paragraphs: In Australia, high property prices and rising cost-of-living pressures are forcing more families to live together under one roof. Many young adults are postponing or completely abandoning their plans to buy their first homes.

As a result, the number of multigenerational households grew by 22% between 2016 and 2021, and experts expect this trend to accelerate. To cope with these financial challenges, older generations are adapting their homes. Some grandparents are renovating their houses to accommodate adult grandchildren, while others are buying modular homes to place on their children’s land.

Many families find positive benefits in this arrangement, such as shared living costs and built-in help with childcare. In response to this demand, secondary dwellings such as granny flats are becoming increasingly popular. Industry leaders are now calling for simpler planning laws to make it easier to build these small homes across the country.

words.d: to give up on something completely or leave it behind
involving several generations of a family living or working together
a house, apartment, or other place where people live

paragraphs: Houses are very expensive in Australia, so many young people cannot buy their first home. Because of high living costs, more generations are deciding to live together in one house.

Between 2016 and 2021, the number of families living this way increased by 22%. Grandparents are helping by rebuilding their homes or adding small houses in their backyards. This arrangement brings many benefits. Families save money, and parents get extra help with child care.
To help more people, industry experts want the government to change building rules. They want it to be easier for families to build small extra houses, called granny flats, in their backyards.

words.d: an open area behind a house, usually covered with grass or a garden
a plan between people about how something will work or be
a good or helpful result of something

paragraphs: Houses in Australia are very expensive today. Young people cannot buy their own homes. Because of this, many families live together in one big house.

Grandparents, parents, and adult children share space to save money. Some older people build small homes in their children’s gardens. Living together helps everyone. Grandparents help with children, and young people get a cheap place to live.
The number of families living together is growing fast every year. Between 2016 and 2021, it goes up by 22%.

words.d: when something costs a lot of money
a person who is not a child anymore
